question:
Select the option that is related to the fourth letter cluster in the same way as the first letter cluster is related to the second letter cluster and fifth letter cluster is related to sixth letter cluster.

SM : UQ :: ? : MT :: CX : EB
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. KP.

GIVEN

• SM : UQ :: ? : MT :: CX : EB

SOLUTION

• The rule (first→second): letters change by +2, +4.

• SM → S+2=U, M+4=Q = UQ ✓

• CX → C+2=E, X+4=B (24+4=28-26=2) = EB ✓

• Here the answer (?) is related to MT the same way: ?+2,+4 = MT.

• So ? = M−2=K, T−4=P = KP.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Reverse the +2/+4 shift on the known pair MT → subtract 2 and 4 → KP.

NOTE

• Use A=1…Z=26 with wrap-around (after Z go back to A) for +/- letter shifts.

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

ZB, VW, RR, NM, JH, ?, BX, XS
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. FC.

GIVEN

• ZB, VW, RR, NM, JH, ?, BX, XS

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: Z(26), V(22), R(18), N(14), J(10), ?, B(2), X(24) → decreasing by 4 → 10−4=6=F.

• 2nd letters: B(2), W(23), R(18), M(13), H(8), ?, X(24), S(19) → decreasing by 5 → 8−5=3=C.

• Missing term = FC.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• First letters −4 each, second letters −5 each; apply once to JH → FC.

NOTE

• When a value goes below A, wrap: 2−4 → 24 = X (mod 26).

question:
A series is given with one term missing. Select the correct alternative from the given ones that will complete the series.

AM, ?, WJ, UG, SC, QX, OR, MK
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. YL.

GIVEN

• AM, ?, WJ, UG, SC, QX, OR, MK

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: A(1), ?, W(23), U(21), S(19), Q(17), O(15), M(13) → −2 each → 1−2=−1=25=Y.

• 2nd letters: M(13), ?, J(10), G(7), C(3), X(24), R(18), K(11) → differences −1, −2, −3, −4, −5, −6, −7 → 13−1=12=L.

• Missing term = YL.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• 1st letter −2 pattern; 2nd letter drops by increasing gaps (−1,−2,−3…). First gap after M is −1 → L.

NOTE

• Watch for arithmetic-progression differences in the second column, not a constant step.

question:
In the following question, set of letter clusters are given. The letter clusters of each set are related to the letter clusters of the same set by some Logic/Rule/Relation. From the given alternatives, select a group of letter clusters which follows the same Logic/Rule/Relation.

(LQ, IN, EJ)

(DN, AK, WG)
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. (FO, CL, YH).

GIVEN

• Sample sets: (LQ, IN, EJ) and (DN, AK, WG).

SOLUTION

• Across the three clusters BOTH letters decrease by 3 then 4, and the gap between the two letters of each cluster stays constant.

• (LQ,IN,EJ): first L(12),I(9),E(5) → −3,−4; second Q,N,J → −3,−4; gap = +5 constant.

• Check option (FO,CL,YH): first F(6),C(3),Y(25) → −3,−4; second O(15),L(12),H(8) → −3,−4; gap = +9 constant ✓.

• Others fail the −3,−4 progression (e.g. VI,SG,MB gives −3,−6).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Just test the first letters of each set for the −3, −4 step; only (FO, CL, YH) fits (6→3→25).

NOTE

• In cluster-set questions check the step between corresponding letters across clusters, plus the internal gap.

question: What will be the sum of the number of Saturdays in the months of October and December in the year 2008?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 8.

GIVEN

• Year 2008 (leap year). Count Saturdays in October and December.

SOLUTION

• 1 Jan 2008 = Tuesday. Days from 1 Jan to 1 Oct = 274 → 274 mod 7 = 1 → 1 Oct 2008 = Wednesday.

• Oct (31 days) from Wed: Saturdays = 4, 11, 18, 25 → 4 Saturdays.

• 1 Dec 2008 = 335 days after 1 Jan → 335 mod 7 = 6 → Tue+6 = Monday.

• Dec (31 days) from Mon: Saturdays = 6, 13, 20, 27 → 4 Saturdays.

• Sum = 4 + 4 = 8.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• A 31-day month gives 5 of a weekday only if that day is among its first 3 dates; here Saturday isn't, so 4 each → 8.

NOTE

• Reference day: 1 Jan 2008 = Tuesday (2008 is a leap year, so add 2 odd days per year normally).

question: Which of the following pairs of years have identical calendars?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 1930 and 1941.

GIVEN

• Find the pair of years with the same calendar.

SOLUTION

• Two years have identical calendars when the odd days between them total 0 (and both are the same type, leap/ordinary).

• From 1930 to 1940 (11 years) leap years are 1932, 1936, 1940 = 3.

• Odd days = 11 + 3 = 14 → 14 mod 7 = 0.

• 1930 and 1941 are both ordinary years → calendars are identical.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• For an ordinary year, its calendar repeats after +6, +11, +11 years. 1930 + 11 = 1941.

NOTE

• Odd days = (number of years) + (number of leap years in the gap); make it a multiple of 7 for a repeat.

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. the ladder with three full cross-rungs.

GIVEN

• Figure 1 : Figure 2 :: Figure 3 : ?

SOLUTION

• Going from the first figure to the second, the internal ladder gains an extra horizontal rung and the cross-bars extend to span the box.

• Applying the same change to the third figure (a two-rung form) produces a three-rung ladder with full-width bars.

• Only Option shows this three-rung, full-width ladder; the others have too few rungs or the wrong spine position.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Count the rungs and note the direction/extent of the bars; pick the figure that adds one rung and completes the bars.

NOTE

• In figure analogies, track one changing feature at a time (here: number of rungs and bar length).

question: Two figures given on the left side of (::) are related with some logic/rule/relation. Select the missing figure on the right side of (::) from the given alternatives based on the same logic/rule/relation.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option.

GIVEN

question:
Select the option that is related to the fifth letter-number cluster in the same way as the second letter-number cluster is related to the first letter-number cluster and fourth letter-number cluster is related to third letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

AF210 : BG238:: KM130 : LN158 :: OR160 : ?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. PS188.

GIVEN

• AF210 : BG238 :: KM130 : LN158 :: OR160 : ?

SOLUTION

• Rule (first→second): each letter +1, number +28.

• AF210 → A+1=B, F+1=G, 210+28=238 = BG238 ✓

• KM130 → K+1=L, M+1=N, 130+28=158 = LN158 ✓

• OR160 → O+1=P, R+1=S, 160+28=188 = PS188.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• +1 to both letters, +28 to the number applied to OR160 → PS188.

NOTE

• Treat the number as a whole (160+28); never split its digits.

question:
Select the option that is related to the first letter-number cluster in the same way as the fourth letter-number cluster is related to the third letter-number cluster and sixth letter-number cluster is related to fifth letter-number cluster. (NOTE: Operations should be performed on the whole numbers, without breaking down the numbers into its constituent digits. E.g.13 – Operations on 13 such as adding /subtracting /multiplying etc. to 13 can be performed. Breaking down 13 into 1 and 3 and then performing mathematical operations on 1 and 3 is not allowed)

PQT14 : ? :: RSW17 : SVB324 :: AKL20 : BNQ441
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. QTY225.

GIVEN

• PQT14 : ? :: RSW17 : SVB324 :: AKL20 : BNQ441

SOLUTION

• Rule (third→fourth): letters +1, +3, +5; number becomes (n+1)².

• RSW17 → R+1=S, S+3=V, W+5=B, (17+1)²=324 = SVB324 ✓

• AKL20 → A+1=B, K+3=N, L+5=Q, (20+1)²=441 = BNQ441 ✓

• PQT14 → P+1=Q, Q+3=T, T+5=Y, (14+1)²=225 = QTY225.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Shift letters by +1/+3/+5 and square (number+1): 14→15²=225 → QTY225.

NOTE

• The number rule here is (n+1)², not a simple addition — verify with both sample pairs.

question: In a certain coded language 'BUSS' is coded as 'CXQN' and 'ANDS' is coded as 'BQBN'. How will 'VEIN' be coded in the same code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. WHGI.

GIVEN

• BUSS → CXQN and ANDS → BQBN.

SOLUTION

• Position-wise letter shifts are +1, +3, −2, −5.

• Check ANDS: A+1=B, N+3=Q, D−2=B, S−5=N = BQBN ✓.

• VEIN → V+1=W, E+3=H, I−2=G, N−5=I = WHGI.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Memorise the shift pattern +1,+3,−2,−5 and apply to V,E,I,N.

NOTE

• Each letter position can have its own fixed shift; derive it from the given words.

question: In a certain coded language 'ANNAS' is coded as 'ESMXN' and 'METAL' is coded as 'QJSXG'. How will 'BUBBA' be coded in the same code language?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. FZAYV.

GIVEN

• ANNAS → ESMXN and METAL → QJSXG.

SOLUTION

• Position-wise letter shifts are +4, +5, −1, −3, −5.

• Check METAL: M+4=Q, E+5=J, T−1=S, A−3=X, L−5=G = QJSXG ✓.

• BUBBA → B+4=F, U+5=Z, B−1=A, B−3=Y, A−5=V (1−5=−4→22=V) = FZAYV.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Apply the fixed shifts +4,+5,−1,−3,−5 to B,U,B,B,A → FZAYV.

NOTE

• Use wrap-around for negative results: A−5 → V (mod 26).

question:
A series is given with one term wrong. Select that wrong term from the given alternatives.

WP547, RN654, ML761, HI860, CH975, XF1082
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. HI860.

GIVEN

• WP547, RN654, ML761, HI860, CH975, XF1082

SOLUTION

• 1st letters: W,R,M,H,C,X → −5 each ✓.

• 2nd letters: P(16),N(14),L(12),?,H(8),F(6) → −2 each, so 4th should be J(10), but it is I(9) → wrong.

• Numbers: 547, 654, 761, ?, 975, 1082 → +107 each, so 4th should be 868, but it is 860 → wrong.

• So the wrong term is HI860 (correct would be HJ868).

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• The number jump should be constant +107; 761→860 is only +99, exposing the wrong term.

NOTE

• Cross-check both the letter step and the number step to locate the odd term.

question: At what time (approximately) (in PM) between 1 PM and 2 PM will the hour and minute hands of the clock be opposite to each other?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 1:38.

GIVEN

• Time between 1 PM and 2 PM when the hands are opposite (180° apart).

SOLUTION

• Angle between hands = |30H − 5.5M|, set equal to 180 with H = 1.

• 5.5M − 30 = 180 → 5.5M = 210 → M = 210 / 5.5 = 38.18 ≈ 38 min.

• So the hands are opposite at about 1:38.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• For hands opposite at H o'clock: M = (5H + 30) × 12/11 = 35 × 12/11 ≈ 38 min past 1.

NOTE

• Minute hand gains on the hour hand at 5.5° per minute; 180° gap gives the opposite position.

question: A clock is 8 minutes fast at 2:00 PM and 14 minutes fast at 8:00 PM. At what time (in AM) will it show the correct time?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 6:00.

GIVEN

• Clock is 8 min fast at 2:00 PM and 14 min fast at 8:00 PM.

SOLUTION

• From 2 PM to 8 PM (6 hours) it gains 14 − 8 = 6 min → 1 min per hour.

• At 2 PM it is already 8 min fast, so it was correct 8 hours earlier.

• 2:00 PM − 8 hours = 6:00 AM.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Gain rate = 6 min / 6 hr = 1 min/hr; roll back the 8-min error → 8 hours before 2 PM = 6 AM.

NOTE

• 'Correct time' is when the accumulated error is 0; move back by (error ÷ rate).

question: In the following figure series, select the figure which can be placed at the sign of question mark (?) from the given alternatives.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. five small squares along the left side.

GIVEN

• A series of boxes with an increasing number of small squares.

SOLUTION

• Number of squares increases by one each step: 1, 2, 3, 4, so the 5th figure has 5 squares.

• The side alternates: box1 left, box2 right, box3 left, box4 right → box5 is on the left.

• Hence the answer is a box with 5 squares stacked on the left side = Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Count = position number (5), and odd positions sit on the left → 5 squares on the left.

NOTE

• In figure series, track both the count and the alternating position of the shapes.

question: In the following figure series, select the figure which can be placed at the sign of question mark (?) from the given alternatives.
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. top row N O R, middle L, bottom P.

GIVEN

• Boxes with the five letters L, N, O, P, R shifting through fixed positions.

SOLUTION

• Reading positions as (top-left, top-centre, top-right, middle, bottom), each step moves letters by the fixed map: pos1→2, pos2→3, pos3→5, pos4→1, pos5→4.

• Figure 4 is O R P / N / L. Applying the map → N O R (top), L (middle), P (bottom).

• That arrangement is N O R / L / P = Option.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Track one letter (e.g. P): its cell cycles the same way each box; extend one more step to fix the layout.

NOTE

• For rotating-letter figures, follow the positional cycle rather than the reading order.

question: The average age of a person and his son at present is 20 years. The ratio of their present ages is 7 : 1. What is the age of son?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 5 years.

GIVEN

• Average age of person and son = 20 → sum = 40. Ratio of ages = 7 : 1.

SOLUTION

• Let ages be 7x and x → 7x + x = 40 → 8x = 40 → x = 5.

• Son's age = x = 5 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• Total = average × 2 = 40; smaller ratio part = 40 × (1/8) = 5.

NOTE

• Average of two numbers × 2 = their sum; then split by the ratio.

question: Sum of the present ages of A, B and C is 110 years. 22 years ago from the present the ratio of ages of A, B and C was 4 : 5 : 2. What is the sum of present ages of A and C?
solution_text:
The correct answer is: Option i.e. 68 years.

GIVEN

• A + B + C (present) = 110. 22 years ago ratio A : B : C = 4 : 5 : 2.

SOLUTION

• 22 years ago total = 110 − 3×22 = 110 − 66 = 44.

• Ratio parts 4 + 5 + 2 = 11 → 1 part = 44 / 11 = 4.

• Ages 22 yrs ago: A = 16, C = 8. Present: A = 38, C = 30.

• Sum of present ages of A and C = 38 + 30 = 68 years.

Therefore, the correct answer is: Option.

SHORT TRICK

• (A+C) then = (4+2) parts = 6×4 = 24; add 2×22 = 44 for present → 68.

NOTE

• For n people, subtract n×(years) from the total to shift everyone back in time.
